name: Segment Comparison
description: A comparative report for ranking segments, explaining contribution, and examining how composition changes across a second dimension or time.

data_requirements.description: The primary measure aggregated and ranked across a comparison dimension.
calculation_hints: Retain top segments and group the remainder as Other when appropriate.

fallback.message: Segment comparison requires at least two comparable categories.

data_requirements.description: Each segment's contribution to the total primary measure.
calculation_hints: Calculate shares against the same filtered population used for ranking.

fallback.message: Omit share calculations when the total is zero or undefined.

data_requirements.description: The primary measure across segment and a secondary dimension or time period.
calculation_hints: Limit both dimensions to readable cardinalities.
Use a consistent population across groups.

fallback.message: Use a table when the dimensional combination is not readable as a chart.

sections.title: Comparison Summary
sections.purpose: Explain the leading and lagging segments and the size of the gap.

blocks.title: Comparison Metrics
instructions: Show the leader, laggard, absolute gap, and relative gap when valid.
Describe comparisons without inferring causality from ranking alone.

sections.title: Segment Ranking
sections.purpose: Make differences in magnitude across segments easy to compare.

blocks.title: Ranked Segments

chart_slot.intent: Rank segments by the primary measure and make magnitude differences easy to compare.

fallback.message: Show the segment ranking as a table.

instructions: Use a horizontal bar layout when segment labels are long.

blocks.title: Segment Contribution
instructions: Include measure, share, rank, and data-quality warnings.

sections.title: Composition Detail
sections.purpose: Show how a secondary dimension contributes within each leading segment.

blocks.title: Segment Composition

chart_slot.intent: Compare the composition of the primary measure across segments and a secondary dimension.

fallback.message: Show the segment-by-dimension breakdown as a table.

instructions: Avoid stacked bars when there are too many secondary categories; prefer heatmap or table fallback.
State which observed gaps deserve investigation rather than claiming an unobserved cause.
